h1: Koh Larn Cafes — 10 Spots Worth the Ferry Ride
intro: For most visitors, Koh Larn means Tawaen Beach at full capacity — rows of beach chairs and seafood grilled by the sand. But this little island, only about 45 minutes by boat from Pattaya, has been quietly growing a cafe scene of its own: beachfront spots where the sea sits right in front of your table, hillside perches looking down over wide bays, and small shops tucked away in the island's back lanes.
heroCredit: Illustrative photo: cafe · Andy Li / Wikimedia (CC0)
quickAnswerHtml: Koh Larn hides more good cafes than most day-trippers realise. This guide covers 10 verified cafes across the island — beachfront tables, hillside sea views and small village spots. Take the 30-baht ferry from Bali Hai Pier in Pattaya (about 45 minutes), rent a motorbike, and you can cover them all in one day trip.

blocks.html: We've narrowed it down to 10 cafes confirmed to be open and operating, based on research and reviews from people who have actually been. There's a mood for every hour of the day — a sea-view table if that's what you're after, shade under the trees if you're escaping the heat, or a slow afternoon that ends with a drink by the water at sunset. Best of all, Koh Larn is small: one rented motorbike is enough to loop the whole list in a single day.

items.name: Fat Submarine Cafe
items.blurb: A beachfront cafe in the Na Ban market strip, a few minutes' walk from the main pier. Tropical decor with hammocks and a rooftop deck over the sea — but what reviewers talk about most are the resident cats strutting around in tiny outfits. Popular orders include the signature Submarine coffee and Nama Banana Choc, with most drinks under 100 baht. Note there's no air-con, so midday gets warm.
items.meta: Na Ban market, near the main pier · Open 09:00–19:00

items.name: Maharak Cafe
items.blurb: A long-running favorite on Na Ban beach, about 400 m from the pier, with a second-floor balcony looking straight out to sea. The owner bakes fresh pastries daily, and 150+ Wongnai reviews mostly praise the vibe and fair prices for a tourist area. In the evening it shifts into a small bar with live music — timed nicely for sunset.
items.meta: Na Ban beach, ~400 m from the pier · Open 10:00–23:00 (closed Wed)

items.name: Matata Bay Cafe
items.blurb: A Bali-style cafe on the road to Ta Yai beach, perched on a low cliff with sea views stretching to the Pattaya skyline. There are two zones — up on the cliff and down on the sand — with seating from floor cushions to beach loungers. Reviewers mention the coconut smoothie and iced coffee; prices run higher than the mainland, which is the going rate for this view. Pets are welcome.
items.meta: Road to Ta Yai beach · Open 09:00–19:00
items.price: Iced coffee from ฿140 · Italian soda ฿120

items.name: Deep Mountain Café
items.blurb: A hilltop cafe in the middle of the island, on the left as you climb toward Samae beach. It serves the high-angle panoramic sea view the beachfront places can't, with vintage knick-knacks throughout and both indoor and garden seating. Reviewers rate the specialty coffee and homemade desserts. A natural rest stop if you're circling the island by motorbike.
items.meta: Hilltop, on the way up to Samae beach · Open 08:30–18:00

items.name: Never Too Small
items.blurb: A tiny cafe near the Na Ban pier with warm white-and-wood decor and lovely light filtering through glass-block walls. Reviewers rave about the house-baked goods — salted caramel croffles, pistachio croissants — and playful drinks like the espresso yuzu soda. Drinks start at 65 baht. A good last stop before catching the ferry back.

items.name: Pakron Cafe
items.blurb: A white timber summer house of a cafe near the Na Ban pier — the name 'Pakron' literally means escaping the heat, which is exactly what it's for. Comfortable inside, with enough photo corners that it's become a default first check-in for people fresh off the boat. Reviewers order the dirty coffee, brownie milkshake and acai bowl. Closed Thursdays.
items.meta: Near Na Ban pier · Open 09:00–17:30 (closed Thu)

items.name: Indigo Cafe
items.blurb: A white-toned cafe fronting Rimtalay Resort on the way to Ta Yai beach. Its claim to fame is the white seaside staircase that photographs like you're standing in the sky. There's an air-conditioned room, a rooftop and waterside seating, and the jellyfish logo has earned it the nickname 'the jellyfish cafe'. Reviewers mention the blueberry cake and orange coffee. Closed Mon–Tue.
items.meta: At Rimtalay Resort, road to Ta Yai beach · Open 09:00–21:00 (closed Mon–Tue)

items.name: Sea You Again Cafe House
items.blurb: The island's only 2D cartoon-themed cafe — a white building traced in black outlines, like walking into a comic book. It sits on a rise beside the main cross-island road, an easy stop between beaches. Inside you get cold air-con and chubby cats lounging around; reviewers typically order the honey toast and cocoa. Reviews from early 2026 show it's still going strong.
items.meta: On the main cross-island road · Open 09:00–20:30

items.name: Kohlarn Coffee Camp
items.blurb: An open-air camping-themed cafe about 300 m from the Na Ban pier, with tents, camp chairs and shaded corners to settle into. Reviewers like the americano list with several variations and the blueberry cheese pie, and there's proper food like fried chicken rice too. Open early till evening — works for both ferry waits and long sits.
items.meta: ~300 m from Na Ban pier · Open 07:30–21:00

items.name: Vibe Bar Kohlarn
items.blurb: A beach-cabin cafe-bar at the far right end of Tawaen beach. It's a coffee shop by day, and by late afternoon people stake out seats for the 5:30–7pm sunset, which several reviews call one of the best vantage points on the beach. The yuzu coffee and homemade pizza get the most mentions; drinks run about 80–200 baht. Closed Thursdays.
items.meta: Tawaen beach (far right end) · Open 07:00–23:00 (closed Thu)

blocks.html: The first ferry leaves Bali Hai Pier around 7:00 am — catch an early boat and make a cafe your first stop if you want a sea-view seat before the crowds land. The last ferry off the island leaves around 6:00 pm, so get to the pier 20-30 minutes early, especially on weekends when the queue gets long.

items: From Bangkok, take a bus or minivan from Ekkamai or Mo Chit to Pattaya (about 2-2.5 hours), then head to Bali Hai Pier at the end of Walking Street in South Pattaya.
The ferry from Bali Hai Pier to Koh Larn costs 30 baht and takes around 35-45 minutes, with departures to both Na Baan Pier and Tawaen Beach; the first boat leaves around 7:00 am.
In a hurry? Speedboats make the crossing in about 15 minutes — roughly 150 baht per person on a shared boat, or charter one as a group.
For the return, the last ferry off the island leaves around 6:00 pm — double-check the timetable at the pier, as schedules can shift with the season.

blocks.html: The cafes are scattered around different corners of the island, so renting a motorbike near Na Baan Pier (roughly 250-400 baht a day) is the easiest way to hop between them. Some island roads are steep, though — if you're not a confident rider, motorbike taxis and songthaews are the safer choice.

faq.q: Can you do Koh Larn's cafes as a one-day trip?
faq.a: Easily — catch a morning ferry, rent a motorbike, and you can comfortably fit in 3-4 cafes plus beach time. Just be back at the pier before the last ferry, around 6:00 pm.

faq.q: Where do you catch the boat to Koh Larn, and how much is it?
faq.a: From Bali Hai Pier in South Pattaya. The ferry costs 30 baht and takes about 35-45 minutes; speedboats do it in around 15 minutes.

faq.q: How do you get between cafes on the island?
faq.a: Renting a motorbike near the pier is easiest, at roughly 250-400 baht a day. Motorbike taxis and songthaews also run regularly from the main beaches.
